issues.issue_title: stm32f412cx: lack of MCO2 bits definition
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: stm32f412cx: lack of MCO2 bits definition
Context: repo=cmsis_device_f4, mcu_series=F4, board=STM32F412CX, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=9
Root cause: Is there any plan to take care of this issue?
Fix: According to RM0402, all STM32F412 chips can configure MCO2 in RCC_CFGR register.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: F4, STM32F412CX, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, cmsis, RM0402, STM32F412, MCO2, RCC_CFGR, cmsis_device_f4

Technical details:
According to RM0402, all STM32F412 chips can configure MCO2 in RCC_CFGR register. The [stm32f412cx.h](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_f4/blob/master/Include/stm32f412cx.h#L8485) header doesn't have the definition of MCO2 bits. I guess it is done this way because all stm32f412cx chips are in UFQFPN48 package, which doesn't have PC9 pin (MCO2 pin). The problem is that changing the MCO2 source clock(to a clock that is disabled) [reduces](https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-products/stm32412cg-ufqfpn48-mco2-unexpected-power-consumption/m-p/622027) power consumption. Wouldn't it make sense to define the MCO2 bits for all STM32F412 bit despite the fact the PC9 pin is not present?

Key comments:
Is there any plan to take care of this issue? ST Internal Reference: 170618 Fixed in commit 2e1724e592931693ce4dfc43e2fd6b3bc375d6a0 Thanks.

issues.issue_title: inconsistent naming of macros accross families
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: inconsistent naming of macros accross families
Context: repo=cmsis_device_f4, mcu_series=F4, board=None, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=low, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=8
Root cause: Hello @maribu, Thank you for this report.
Fix: It seems that the GPIO peripheral is largely the same for all but the STM32F1 family.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: F4, bug_report, low, bug, internal bug tracker, cmsis, GPIO, STM32F1, GPIO_OSPEEDER_OSPEED0, STM32L0, GPIO_OSPEEDER_OSPEEDR0, STM32F0

Technical details:
It seems that the GPIO peripheral is largely the same for all but the STM32F1 family. Still, macros that seem to refer to the exact same thing are named inconsistently, e.g.: - GPIO_OSPEEDER_OSPEED0: STM32L0 - GPIO_OSPEEDER_OSPEEDR0: STM32F0, STM32F2, STM32F3, STM32F4, STM32F7, STM32G4, STM32L1, STM32L4 - GPIO_OSPEEDR_OSPEED0: STM32F2, STM32F4, STM32G0, STM32G4, STM32L4, STM32L5, STM32U5, STM32WB, STM32WL - GPIO_OSPEEDR_OSPEEDR0: STM32F0, STM32F7 Are there any plans to at least provide aliases (e.g. #define GPIO_OSPEEDR_OSPEED0 GPIO_OSPEEDER_OSPEEDR0) so that there is one canonical name for each macro that works across families?

Key comments:
Hello @maribu, Thank you for this report. We will get back to you as soon as we analyze it further. This may take some time. Thank you for your comprehension. ST Internal Reference: 179423 ST Internal Reference: 179424 ST Internal Reference: 179452 Hello @maribu, Thank you for your feedback about the inconsistent GPIO macro names across STM32 families. After your request, we reviewed our series and updated our drivers to match the official documentation. However, we currently do not plan to add extra macros or aliases to make the naming consistent across all families. We understand this can make code portability more difficult, and we appreciate your suggestion. For now, there are no plans to add these aliases, so we will close this issue. Thank you for your understanding.

Problem: Typo in definition of __STM32F4xx_CMSIS_VERSION
Context: repo=cmsis_device_f4, mcu_series=F4, board=STM32F4XX, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=low, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=6
Root cause: Hi @svijsv, The issue you pointed out has been confirmed, a fix will be implemented and made available in future release.
Fix: The definition of __STM32F4xx_CMSIS_VERSION in stm32f4xx.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: F4, STM32F4XX, bug_report, low, internal bug tracker, cmsis

Technical details:
The definition of __STM32F4xx_CMSIS_VERSION in stm32f4xx.h reads #define __STM32F4xx_CMSIS_VERSION ((__STM32F4xx_CMSIS_VERSION_MAIN << 24)\ |(__STM32F4xx_CMSIS_VERSION_SUB1 << 16)\ |(__STM32F4xx_CMSIS_VERSION_SUB2 << 8 )\ |(__STM32F4xx_CMSIS_VERSION)) resulting in a compilation error when used. It should instead read #define __STM32F4xx_CMSIS_VERSION ((__STM32F4xx_CMSIS_VERSION_MAIN << 24)\ |(__STM32F4xx_CMSIS_VERSION_SUB1 << 16)\ |(__STM32F4xx_CMSIS_VERSION_SUB2 << 8 )\ |(__STM32F4xx_CMSIS_VERSION_RC))

Key comments:
Hi @svijsv, The issue you pointed out has been confirmed, a fix will be implemented and made available in future release. Thank you once again for your contribution. ST Internal Reference: 110625 I suggest to close this issue because it was fixed months ago. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_f4/blob/7ac69098b3e5f9b2d929acd4f087e92a7e59e0e9/Include/stm32f4xx.h#L110-L117 Hi @svijsv, As this issue has been fixed please allow me then to close this thread. Thank you again for your contribution.
